name: Putharo
ingredients: Rice flour (specifically local sticky or red rice flour)
instructions: 1. Mix rice flour with a pinch of salt and enough water to form a smooth, thick batter that is spreadable but not runny.
2. Heat a specialized clay pot (or a flat-bottomed pan) over medium heat and lightly grease it.
3. Pour a ladleful of the batter into the center of the pot and spread it evenly.
4. Cover the pot with a lid and let it steam-cook until the surface is dry and the edges pull away slightly from the sides.
5. Once firm and cooked through, carefully remove the Putharo and serve warm.
description: Putharo is a staple breakfast bread of the Pnar and Khasi communities of Meghalaya. It is a simple, comforting rice pancake that is often served alongside spicy meat curries or local tea, reflecting the indigenous reliance on rice as a primary dietary component in the hilly terrain.
